utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We won't keep you long today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer. Please continue with your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I would just like to inform the Chamber of the following: My client cannot attend today's hearing because he hasn't been feeling too well since yesterday. That's the only thing I wanted to inform you about. But we shall continue to -- with the proceedings in order not to disturb the schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. I think we care very much about your client's health. We wish him a speedy recovery. And I was told that he was seen by a doctor yesterday afternoon. I hope we could get some kind of report or review from that doctor to see how the condition is of your client. We'll do everything possible to take care of him. Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Re-examined by Mr. Stringer: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to go to two exhibits, the first of which is Exhibit P4.14. It's been assigned a new number. It's the one that was marked by the witness during his cross-examination yesterday. And also, witness, I'm going to ask the usher to show you a different exhibit which you haven't seen yet, which is a document marked P557. 557. Witness, 557 is not a document you've seen before, although you looked at two very similar ones yesterday during your cross-examination by my learned friend Mr. Seric. This one is dated the 3rd of August, 1993, and it's a report on the military situation in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My learned friend Stringer himself said that this document was not used in cross-examination yesterday, so I think it's only logical for me to object about the question being asked completely out of the scope of the cross-examination and relating purportedly to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, you have to know that the re-examination should be strictly within the scope of the cross-examination and the -- and the -- of course some new documents will be allowed to use so long as it's directly related to the point mentioned in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe it is well within the scope of the cross-examination. I'm referring to two documents that Mr. Seric used yesterday during the cross in which he asked the witness questions about the presence or deployment of the HVO military police in the area that has been marked on the photograph. This document relates to the very same issue, and in fact I think it's more pertinent because it relates specifically to the period of time that we're talking about here, which is early August 1993. So I think if I'm allowed to ask just a few questions about it, it will be evident that this is within the scope of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may try that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I want to direct your attention to page 3 of my version. I'm not sure where this is found on the original language version that you have. I'm looking at a section of this report that falls under the heading of "Second sector." It may be on the second page of that document. Do you see the section called "Second sector"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the second paragraph there starts with the words "On the positions." Do you see that? "On the positions --"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "In the old grammar school up to the health centre, 168 military policemen have been deployed." And then moving down to the next paragraph, it says: "On the position of the health centre, 58 soldiers of ATG Mrmak were deployed." Do you see that also?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just a couple questions on this and then we'll move on to the next topic. First of all, the old grammar school that is referred to in this document, is the old grammar school found on the photograph that you have with you there, 14.4? Do you see the location of the old grammar school in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, actually, I'm not sure which school they're referring to as the old grammar school, but this whole series of buildings were schools, several schools, adjacent buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you worked in this area, did you see members of the HVO military police deployed or manning any part of this section of the Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, there were all sorts of soldiers there. I'm not sure who was a member of the police. In fact, the police had special insignia on their shoulder straps, but there were other soldiers there too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I must object to this question, although it has been asked already, because when the Prosecutor says "this part of the Bulevar," and the witness has drawn a very wide circle, then I don't think the question is very accurate as to which part of the Bulevar exactly the Prosecutor was referring to, because what comes across this way is that soldiers were manning the whole length of the Bulevar, the way the question has been asked, which is quite in contradiction with the document that the witness has before him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think Mr. Stringer is trying to know the deployment of the troops of various kinds of uniforms. Maybe your question is not that pertinent, Mr. Stringer. You may rephrase it in such a way so that to have your idea come across more clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm talking about the area that falls inside the circle that you drew on that photograph. Okay? At any location within that circle, did you see military policemen deployed or manning positions in that area during the time that you were working in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't really see any MP's in that particular part of the Bulevar. They were just regular soldiers. Only during the operation on the 17th of September, yes, there were some. But I was standings outside the Ero Hotel, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked about this gentleman, the military policeman, Mr. Stojanovski. How many times did he bring you to work in this area that you've circled?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have heard in direct examination already and again in cross-examination, so I'm not sure why my learned colleague Stringer should like to repeat the examination-in-chief. This has been said before this court already that every single time Luka Stojanovski was the one to drive him. We've heard that already.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm trying to do a very brief redirect. We discussed Mr. Stojanovski a great deal on the cross-examination. The witness was taken to the logbooks, in which he was signed out by Mr. Stojanovski as well as any number of other units. I'm simply trying to -- I think it's an issue that is legitimate for redirect, and it's a question simple, how many times did Stojanovski take him to this area. I -- I think it's a legitimate question for redirect in view of what was raised in cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The witness has answered that question during the cross-examination. The Defence counsel claims that, you know, the -- the witness answered that question, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I disagree, Mr. President. Again, this goes back to some of the difficulties that I experienced yesterday in terms of the scope of the cross-examination. The scope of the direct examination was very limited to the specific issue regarding the burial, quite frankly, Mr. President. I deliberately did not elicit testimony from the witness about other times that he was brought to these locations, other work that was performed for the Vinko Skrobo unit. This is an area among a number of others that was opened up wide in the cross-examination and I think I ought to be entitled to pursue briefly a few of those areas. Mr. Seric opened the door more generally to the issue of forced labour that this witness was required to perform, and this question falls squarely within the scope of that cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, would it please be possible for the witness to leave the courtroom so then we can discuss a number of issues that is Mr. Stringer has just brought up, and they just aren't true. And again, in his questions this morning, he keeps repeating to the witness something that I don't think is quite correct. So may the witness please be permitted to leave the courtroom so I could bring up a number of points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, of course that's in the cross-examination Mr. Seric brought up many more wider scope of the issues in the cross-examination, but we have made a decision that in the rebuttal proceedings we are only interested in the four areas - that is, the burial of Mr. Harmandzic and other three matters - so even if the question of forced labour was mentioned in the direct or in the cross-examination, this Trial Chamber will not take those testimony into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this issue does relate to Mr. Harmandzic. I can explain that to the Trial Chamber. I think it would -- it should take place outside the presence of the Trial Chamber, but this is an issue that relates to Mr. Harmandzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you believe so, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, it's really just one or two questions on this. Again, Mr. Stojanovski, how many times did he bring you to the area that you've circled on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number of time, but quite often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And among those times that he brought you to this area, did you work for Stela's soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: We worked along the whole length of the line that I've marked from the medical centre all the way up to the school building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there ever times when prisoners were shared between different units, that is, prisoners who had been brought to work for different units might be tasked to work for another unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, actually, every time we were taken to this area, they would split us up into groups and then assign five, seven, or eight people to each of the groups, and then we would be assigned tasks to perform in each of the groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. My question was a little bit different though. Were there times when prisoners came into your group, say, who had been signed out of the Heliodrom by another part of the HVO, a different unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric. What's the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem is that the Prosecutor is leading the witness, and that, we know, is not the right way to question a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The witness has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you were shown the logbook for the 17th of September. And just a few brief questions about that. Where did you work on the 17th of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: We worked just a way down from the Ero Hotel, near Santiceva Street and down onto the Neretva River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your cross-examination by Mr. Seric, you said you were involved in burying bodies then on the following day, the 18th of September; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many bodies were you involved in burying on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 72, 73 bodies, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who those people were, generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of them were prisoners, people from the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know under what circumstances those persons had been killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mostly they were killed during combat operations along the line of separation, because we had been taken there to perform labour and that's where people got killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when they were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same day that we were taken there, the 17th of September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you bury any of your relatives on that day, the 18th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without mentioning any names, can you tell us who that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: My close neighbours, my brother.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, please. Your Honours, as you can see, and I have been observing this for quite a while now. Yes, you can issue an order but the order is modified the way the Prosecutor sees fit, and then we're supposed to be the ones to introduce new topics and justify them. This topic being discussed now is absolutely outside the scope of this testimony and this is not a subject that the Prosecutor can legitimately go into. Now, it was not mentioned in the cross-examination or in the direct examination, and now a new subject is being introduced, and this keeps happening all the time. Well, in that case, I was thinking perhaps tomorrow I may try to reopen an entirely new discussion and a new hearing and maybe that would indeed be necessary the way things are going right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can say, first of all I finished with that subject. Secondly, that issue was raised on the cross-examination over my objection. But the Trial Chamber allowed it, and in any event, I've finished with that and I intend now to move into redirect in response to Mr. Krsnik's cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, the Trial Chamber allowed the Defence counsel to cross-examine the witness on this subject only because we believed this matter related to the credibility of this witness in the cross-examination. We have already made a ruling that we will only hear the testimonies of the witnesses in the four areas, and we will only take those areas into consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I want to now refer you to the cross-examination that was conducted by my learned friend Mr. Krsnik yesterday, who's the lawyer for Mr. Naletilic. First of all, I want to give you the statement that you made in 1996 and then just to ask you a few questions about that. I don't know that it's been marked or given a number. It is the statement of 11 January, 1996. Witness, just a few questions about the circumstances of your giving this statement. What was the format that was used in the interview in which you gave this information? Did they ask you questions, or did you just share with them information that you thought should be shared? How -- what was the format?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, actually, I told them my story, things that had happened to me. The questions were not really very specific. There were a number of questions, but mainly I told them my story, most of what I'd been through, so that's how this statement was made and I later signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ask you about Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 2 of the -- of the English version, you refer to a -- at the bottom of the English version, page 2, you say there were members of Tuta's unit stationed at the Heliodrom. You knew them by sight. I wanted to ask you: How did you know them by sight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we knew them from the days of the events in Sovici, and then they would take us to perform forced labour, to clean their toilets up there and to make their beds, and anything that was necessary, the work to be done for the institution where they were staying. They took us to all the battalions that were stationed there and we performed work there too, the Busicis [phoen] and the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your cross-examination, you also described a training exercise in which your task was to construct a field privy or a field water closet. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What period of time did that training exercise take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly the date, but it was, I think, in March. It was springtime. It may have been March, but springtime at any rate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked about this document or this part of a document that's been marked Exhibit 928/5.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Perhaps we should show that to the witness, 928/5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I just know exactly which document we're talk about, because I didn't use a single document in my cross-examination for this witness. No, I surely wasn't using this document in my cross-examination. I'm sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, just because he didn't use a document in the cross doesn't mean it's not within -- it's not an issue that can be raised in direct -- in redirect. I'm asking, Mr. President -- I'm asking a question to clarify the issue that was raised during the cross-examination. I think the document may assist. It may not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I've been receiving warnings from you for a year, and you have been cautioning me. We know that if the question wasn't asked in cross-examination, it couldn't be used in redirect. You, Your Honours, have told me that at least 20 times. And thirdly, I merely asked what document we were talking about. There must be some set of rules. This is beginning to give me a good laugh. This is supposed to be a serious court. I mean, my apologies, but I really no longer know how to react to these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, according to my remarks, I think this document was used in the direct examination. It was there already.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's a marked exhibit, Mr. President. It's been provided to the Defence. I don't know what more I can do if he doesn't have the documents at hand, it's his own failing, not that of the Prosecutor or the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But you have to inform the Defence counsel what kind of document it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It's the excerpt from the diary related to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am going to be objecting all the time. Obviously I don't have the document, I don't have 400 people waiting in front of the courtroom that I can summon at any moment and ask them to bring me the document. But if I didn't use the document in my cross-examination, I am sure my learned friend cannot use it in the redirect. Maybe we could refer back to the Statute. Maybe we should have used it all the time during the proceedings in order to make things clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, it depends on what kind of subject that the Prosecution is going to ask. It doesn't matter what kind of document the Prosecution is going to use. We will see whether the subject matter is related in the cross-examination or not. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you looked at part of this document during your direct examination. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, I do not understand your question. What was your question about?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you turn to the fourth page of this exhibit, you're going to see some text in your language. Do you recall looking this over during a part of your direct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the other day when you were showing it to me, a day or two days ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, this is my question: During the cross-examination by Mr. Krsnik, you testified about the construction of a field privy on a training exercise. My question is whether that testimony relates to this document -- this training exercise, or did you build that privy at a different time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I object. He has asked that question -- it has been asked and answered. Now, Mr. Stringer is absolutely suggesting a different answer to this witness based on the written document in front of him, and that is wholly improper and I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it is true that this question has been asked in cross-examination, but so we need some -- some points to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't -- I don't think -- I don't think he is -- it's abnormal, you know, for the Prosecution to ask that question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was asked on cross-examination but it was just asked two or three minutes ago on redirect examination, and the witness answered specifically, "It was springtime, March or April." He didn't like the answer, now he's going to put the document in front of him and get the answer he wants with a suggestive and leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, if the witness is going to tell the truth, he will stick to his answer; right? Because in this stage of the re-examination, I don't think any witness could be led.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. String well, I can ask it perhaps a different way, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, looking at this document, the training exercise that's referred to in this document, what was your task on this training -- this training exercise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only task I got was that, and after that I did not get any other special tasks or orders to carry out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And just so we're clear, what is the task that you refer to? What was the task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: My task was to build this field toilet or privy, and then we also brought something to protect the command in Jablanica, and that was all during my work. I stayed there only one day. I came one evening and then left the following evening. I just spent one night there, and that was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your cross-examination you were asked about -- to estimate the height of the man you called Tuta. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not asked whether you could identify other characteristics of this person. Looking at page 4 of the OTP witness statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I remember well, I did not ask for the height of Mr. Tuta here in the courtroom. I asked the witness to estimate my height, my height. And then I asked him how tall was the guy that he called Tuta, and then he told me and I asked him whether this man that he called Tuta was taller than me or about the same height. I didn't ask the witness to estimate Tuta's height at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I did not ask for any other characteristics because the gentleman knows Tuta from TV. He watched him on several shows. Maybe I should have asked him is that the man that you saw on TV, and he watched those shows before he travelled to The Hague according to his own statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. It is true you did not ask the height of Mr. Tuta. You just asked how tall is the man who was called Tuta. That's exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That was my question. That was what I referred to, the testimony in which he was asked to estimate the height of the person he called Tuta. You can read it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, witness, I want to direct your attention or ask you to keep in mind your interview with the OTP investigator from six months ago, April of this year. Okay? Do you recall -- do you recall telling the investigator what the colour of the man's hair was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the colour of the hair that you described for the investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was grey, just the way it is now, greyish, turning grey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any other features that you described to the investigator that you can recall now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had a beard when he came up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the colour of the beard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: A grey beard. The colour of the beard was the same as the colour of the hair.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just a moment ago you said that the colour of the hair is just the way it is now. Did you see that person here, that is, the person you've described as Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any doubts about whether that person that you saw here is the person that you saw in Sovici on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. It was the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions from the Judges? Judge Clark. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yes. I have a few questions. I'll try to confine my questions to the areas which we have directed the counsel towards. I wasn't clear about something yesterday from the questions that were put to you by the Prosecution and then by Mr. Krsnik. Were you a member of both organisations, HVO and the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: When you were in Sovici on the days of the 17th and 18th of April, in 1993, an you described here a man who you've just been describing now as Mr. Tuta, I got the impression that -- well, maybe I shouldn't say that. Did you think that he was playing any role in the events that happened on the 17th and 18th of April in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: From your point of view, who was more important that day in Sovici outside the school, Mr. Tuta or Mr. Rogic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, they were together. Mr. Tuta was in the school office. I was being chased round all the time. They would bring me to the school and then take me back, and every time I came to the school I saw a number of them sitting with Mr. Tuta in that office and I saw a number of men leaning against the wall facing the wall with their arms up in the air.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: That's not quite the question I asked. I think you told us that Mr. Rogic was a magistrate, and obviously you knew him as a person of importance in your community. As far as you were concerned- now - we'll just talk about you now - who was the more important person who had more to do with you that day in Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Rogic was in charge of everything. He made all the initiatives. He gave all the instructions as to what had to be done, so it was Mr. Rogic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Rogic would have known every one of you quite well, is that the situation, being a local?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Now, this may be a difficult question. If you don't know, say so. It just helps me to form a view. Would Mr. Rogic have played a part in identifying to the soldiers from outside the area who was an important player, who was a member of ABiH, who might have been a soldier carrying arms, and who would have been a civilian? Do you understand what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand you very well. I don't know how to answer your question though. I really don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did you get the impression that Mr. Rogic was furnishing information to any of the other outside soldiers about who was who in the village of Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had information. He had his own deployment, and he furnished those to the local commanders who obeyed his orders. That was until the moment we left. Later on how things were then, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think Mr. Seric asked you were you a smoker, and I think he elicited from you that you had to surrender your cigarettes, your lighter, your personal possessions. Did you ever in the period from the time you were first taken in the bus until you were released ever get your personal belongings back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: When you were in the Heliodrom, were you allowed to smoke?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who had cigarettes in the cells, they could smoke. There was no specific ban. But since we didn't have the money to buy cigarettes, the majority of us didn't smoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: If you did have access to cigarettes, how would you light them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was always somebody who managed to hide something in their pockets during the search, so there would always be something handy, some sort of a gadget that we could use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Were you treated when you were a prisoner as a civilian or a soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were all treated as soldiers regardless of how old we were because there were people aged 82 or older with canes, and they were also in the camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Now, if I can bring you to the burial of the first body in Liska Park. Did you mark that particular grave - that would have been your first burial - in any way? Was there anything to indicate that a body was there and the dates that it was buried?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no markings whatsoever on the grave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I ask you when you first -- I'm not asking you the date, but in around what time did you make contact with anybody in authority in relation to the location of this grave in Liska Park?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first contacts with the authority I had when I left the camp, somewhat later. I can't remember the date. That was upon issuing the statement. Everybody who was in the camp issued their statements. When we issued a statement, we were summoned, and that's what happened later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: When you talked about what had happened to you during the period that you were incarcerated, how did -- I'm trying to find out or to establish the link between the burial in Liska Park and the contact with the alleged son of the victim that you buried. You didn't know who it was. There were just the people in the Heliodrom -- were guessing. But at what stage did you make contact with the authorities which led to the exhumation of the body which you had buried?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: The contact was established in 1994, when I was released from the Heliodrom, and the body was exhumed much later than that initial contact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think that you said that you made the statement that has been referred to here in January 1996 in Jablanica, and Mr. Krsnik thinks you made it in Konjic, but there was a debate about that or a discussion. Did you at any stage meet anyone in relation to the body or the burial, or was it before that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a meeting before I gave the statement. The statement was issued subsequently, not in Konjic but in Jablanica. Before I issued the statement, I had contacts regarding the body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Yesterday you made reference to a piece of paper that you had. It wasn't clear to me what you were saying. A piece of paper which appeared to say that you had a little map of where the body would be found and you mentioned something about the Red Cross. I wasn't at all clear about this piece of paper. Could you help me on that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I did not have a piece of paper, but I kept the messages that I received from my folks from Vakuf and I just happened to have those messages in my pocket, and everything that I experienced, all the burials that I attended, I made notes of -- I made the note of location, how the person was dressed. I would also make the note of the row or the number of the grave. And of the 70-something people which were buried in Miljkovici, I had the note of that, how many of them, in what row -- in which row. And if I knew the name, I would make a note of that. If I didn't know, obviously I couldn't make a note of their names. So I made a record of all that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And when you say you didn't have the notes any more, did you give them to the investigating police who were exhuming the bodies? Is that how you lost the notes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That message remained with the Mostar police. It was never returned to me, and it so happened that they have misplaced it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: My final question, then: From what you said, I understood you to mean that you remembered where this body was buried because it was your first burial and it was the only burial in Liska Park. Am I correct in that interpretation of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can remember, I buried just one body there and nobody else in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judge's questions? Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just one question, Mr. President. Further examination by Mr. Stringer:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, your testimony about Mr. Rogic in Sovici -- Judge Clark asked you about his position -- was he acting as a civilian, a judge, or a military man on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: He acted as a civilian, as a judge. He was also the president of the HDZ, and he was a civilian, he had a very nice suit on. He acted as a civilian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was he not wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Further cross-examination by Mr. Seric:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please listen carefully to my question. The body that you buried in Liska Park, was it exhumed from the same hole where you put it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I wasn't present where the body was exhumed. I came to the police and handed over the piece of paper indicating the row and the number. There were people from the exhumation team there and there was security there, and I did not attend the exhumation. I did not come to the grave to point to the grave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you anything about that, what was -- what hole was the body taken out from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody told me anything. They left. I remained waiting there for an hour or so. I can't remember exactly. But when they returned, they said everything was okay, that the man's son identified the body, that the body was the one that they suspected it was, and then they let me go. They took me to Jablanica, and I don't know what else happened. I heard that there was another body there, but I told them immediately that as far as I could remember, there was just one body buried there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, no questions? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to help us. We appreciate that very much. When the usher pulls down the blinds, he will show you out of the room. We all wish you a pleasant journey back home and a good future.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for listening to me carefully. I apologise for not choosing my words very carefully. I apologise for that. And if need may be, I will come back for as many times as necessary to give my evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage are there any documents to tender? Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise. You've caught me off guard. I had forgotten about that issue, which you always ask. If I can just reach for my outline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think there are several maps and photographs used during the -- yes, during the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe Madam Registrar could help us in this aspect.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can assist. On the 7th of October, P6.7/3 was tendered, P6.8/2, P14.4/5, 12 -- excuse me, P12/2, P928/5. And that was all for the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That's consistent with my notes, and I thank the registrar for assistance on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections? Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit 928/5, we absolutely object to that exhibit. The witness is so far -- and this witness today particularly, he'd never seen the document, he's never heard of the man. The content of the document did not corresponded with what the witness was talking about. I no longer know what to say, how to show my disapproval. I'm not sure what the translation was. I would like to use this opportunity to tender two documents we've used into evidence. That's -- oh, excuse me, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll have to do it one by one. Mr. Seric, any objection to those documents tendered by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm only speaking about documents relating to my client, so I'm not talking about documents Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. relating to Mr. Mladen Naletilic. No, no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So the four documents, P6.8/2, P6.7/3, P14.4/5, and P12/2 are admitted into the evidence. As for the document P928/5, this Trial Chamber will make a decision at a later stage. Mr. Krsnik, do you have any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The documents I've used, statement dated 16th of January, Konjic or Jablanica; and then D1/415 and 414. That was a statement that was given to the investigators of the Prosecution. These are the two documents that we would like to please have tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We object to the statement in evidence, Mr. President. I do recall an earlier decision in this case at the beginning of this trial in which the Trial Chamber indicated we would only accept witness statements as going to credibility, as opposed to substantive evidence. But in any case, we object to the admission of the witness statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, why do we ask to tender these exhibits into evidence? In order to confirm the credibility of the witness. And also I would like to draw your attention to the judgement and the final decision in the Kupreskic case, what the Judge wrote there about the final decision concerning the statement given to the AID and their investigators. I would not like to go any further into that now. I would like to remind you of the use of such statements and of the way such statements were used. But I would no longer like to tire you with that. But it's all there in that final decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully support my colleague Krsnik's proposal as if it were our own, concerning these two documents, and additionally I would like to tender into evidence photograph number 14.4. I think the number would be D2/80. And map number D2 -- number 11.18, I think that would be D2/81. So our Defence has four documents to tender into evidence, the four we have just enumerated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As for the photos and the maps, do you have any objections, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So the D2/80 and D2/81 are admitted into the evidence. As for the previous statement of the witness, Mr. Krsnik, and Mr. Seric, I believe that this Trial Chamber has made a decision that all the previous statements and any written documents written by the witness are not admitted into the evidence. This is a Rule from the very beginning of this trial until now, almost last day of this trial. Secondly, Mr. Krsnik, I believe that during your cross-examination you used very extensively that document. I must say almost all the important matters in those two documents are mentioned in the transcript. We believe that's enough to support your case to attack the credibility of that witness, so we decided that these two documents are not admitted into evidence. It is so decided. Well, I would like to know whether the next witness is ready and any protective measures for the next witness. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before the witness enters the courtroom, I would please ask you to help me with this and my colleagues from the Prosecution too. I have a proposal to make. First I would like to ask the Prosecutor the following question: Is it their intention to use this witness who is about to testify to tender into evidence 65 documents listed here and purportedly given by -- provided by the Prosecutor? If so, if they're preparing to tender into evidence those documents, in that case the Defence is not yet ready to cross-examine because we were only given these documents on the 4th of October this year. Another thing I want to emphasise: On the 4th of October this year, the documents we received, we found something there that we think is a very serious issue. We have found a number of exculpatory elements such as General Petkovic's order to release all civilians from Sovici on the 4th of May. Can there possibly be anything more exculpatory as a document than that? And the Prosecution received that document in June of the year 2000, and they failed to hand it over to us until the 4th of October this year. Your Honours, I can keep on enumerating individual statements. I can talk about statements given by witnesses to the AID but not forwarded to us because we've only just received them. I could talk on about this for a very long time, the ways in which the Defence has been prejudiced by such behaviour, but we're preparing a very comprehensive motion in which we will list individual cases of witnesses who is testified here who had given statements to the AID but those statements were not forwarded to us and we could not use it in our cross-examination. Let's learn [As interpreted] all this exculpatory documents and evidence. Your Honours, what would have been if prior to our motion for acquittal we'd had the document that they were supposed to forward to us, because they had received it in the year of 2000, this order by General Petkovic. And you know what my own client is being charged with, with respect to the civilian population. So this is a proposal I wish to make, since my client is not present here today, and this is supposed to be -- the following witness is supposed to be the last witness concerning my client. We have ready to accept Apolonia Bos from the Office of the Prosecutor today and if my client gets better today, perhaps he may be able to attend tomorrow. Also concerning my colleague Bos from the investigation unit, her statement, Your Honours, only related to the so-called rifles. But when the Prosecution asked to have her questioned, they said suddenly she will talk about the diary too. I have a right to know whether she will, and indeed I must prepare for that case. So these are the two proposals I wish to make. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any response? Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, the response is that it's very obvious, starting on Monday morning, that the Defence has very clearly embarked on a course this week to be as difficult and obstreperous as possible at every turn, and that continues just in the last few minutes. All the disclosure that we believe that was required and proper to make has been made all along. The very fact, the very fact that we turned over certain documents next -- last week related to the testimony -- potentially the testimony of witnesses to be called this week, is indeed evidence that we have met and continue to meet our disclosure obligations. As to the next witness and the diary, the Chamber will hear very shortly the witness is going to give only the most basic information to answer various questions the Chamber has had in terms of when the Office of the Prosecutor received certain documents, certain versions, either the B/C/S version or the typed version or whatever of the diary. Certainly simply as a matter of record. I'm looking right now, Your Honour, at my outline, and on the Rados diary for this witness, I think there's six or seven questions. And it's simply as to when was this received, and that's the nature of it. I also would say, Your Honour, that Ms. Bos, because the -- I hope the Chamber will understand -- travels frequently in the region, she's not requesting a pseudonym, she is requesting that her facial image be distorted, again, because she travels frequently in that region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. So the next witness will be Ms. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Bos, Your Honour. And she's not asking for a pseudonym. We can refer to her as we already have, by name, but she wants her face to be protected, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric. Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this assertion by Mr. Scott, I find I have to react to it. The Defence isn't employing any sort of strategy. We only have a heart and a desire to do -- to perform our task as well as we can. At least give us an illusion that our work is not in vain, please. We are not lawyers from the United States. We are not from Great Britain, we are not from any of those really big and important states. But believe me, our law faculty in Zagreb is a lot older than many cities in the United States.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I see no objections from Defence counsel concerning with the protective measures of Ms. Bos. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No objection concerning that. But even so, Your Honour, I must appeal to justice. I cannot have a witness by the Prosecution without having received a statement previously. I have only just found out that this witness was going to give testimony about the Rados diary three days ago. Please, these are the very last witnesses. Does not the Defence team have the right to know that the Rados diary was going to be discussed? Well, then I really don't know what to say. Let her then give testimony about this part of the statement that we do have and that we have read, and please may I have a statement prepared concerning the testimony about the Rados diary. Please, Your Honours, allow us to have that at least, because we have to defend our client. There's a witness appearing now, and I have no idea what she's going to talk about. She hasn't been announced and we don't even have here statement. And they call it obstacles. Just because we are seeking justice and equality. The Prosecutor seems to think that that's not obstacle. Well, maybe he really does find that it's an obstacle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think this Trial Chamber made a decision on the 20th of September concerning of the areas in the rebuttal proceedings. We specifically identified three or four areas that the witness testimony in those four fields are allowed; that is, the events related to Sovici and Doljani, the burial of Mr. Harmandzic, the identification of the wooden rifle, as well as the Rados diary. We know the position of that witness. She is an investigator in the OTP. She was not the writer of that diary. Many events -- most of the events in the -- mentioned in that diary, she'll know next to nothing. She's just going to tell us how the OTP got that diary. It's very simple. And Mr. Scott promised us he'll only have five or six questions concerning the Rados diary. This Trial Chamber has made a decision today, allowed Ms. Bos to be called to testify in the rebuttal, and her testimony shall be limited to the two matters. One is identification of the wooden rifle; and the other is the Rados diary. I see no objections against the protective measures asked by the Prosecution, so that protective measure is granted. Could we have the witness, please. And by the way, Mr. Par, we looked into the jurisdiction about the submission of the final briefs. We found that on a certain date all the final briefs should be submitted in the language used -- officially used by this Tribunal. That is English or French. We made the decision for the deadline almost a month ago. I think both parties have enough time to draft it and have it translated into the official language of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have understood your decision, but our intention is to appeal against this decision because we believe that the quality of arms of the sides has been -- has not been just. We believe that the Prosecution has had more time for the final brief than we were given, and I would just like to reiterate this view on our part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we will take note of your remarks. Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Scott:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Bos, will you state your full name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Apolonia Adriana Bos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Ms. Bos as you may know, I'm not sure how the monitor might be arranged. But in any event, your request to have your facial image protected has been granted and is being protected.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, very, very briefly, Ms. Bos. You are an investigator with the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long have you been a -- excuse me, an investigator with the Office of the Prosecutor here?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Since June 1995, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you a police officer or investigator with a Dutch police force for a number of years before that?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally by way of background, just so the record is clear, is it correct, Ms. Bos, that your native language is Dutch but you feel comfortable to give your testimony in English? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the first topic I want to direct your attention to, Ms. Bos, and I'm hoping we can move rather quickly, is a document that has become known -- and I'll simply use the terminology -- the Rados diary. Can you advice the Chamber if you've had a chance to determine when a typed, what we call B/C/S, version of that diary was received by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: According to the records of the Tribunal, that was submitted to the Tribunal on the 16th of March, 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you also been able to determine when the Office of the Prosecutor first received a copy of the handwritten, now distinguishing, the handwritten version of that diary?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: A copy of the handwritten version was received on the 10th of September -- sorry, 10th of December, 1998.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And since that time and in recent days has the Office of the Prosecutor been able to obtain the original of that diary?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's correct. Since recently we have been able to obtain the original diary. That was on the 24th of September when it was given to my colleague Brett Pakenham. He brought it into the Tribunal when he travelled back, which was on the 25th, 26th of September, this year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the usher's assistance to provide what's been marked as Exhibit 928C to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: At line 12 the witness mentioned my colleague, but the record does not show the name. Could possibly she repeat that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's -- if I can assist. It's Brett Pakenham. B-R-E-T-T. Excuse me for the mispronunciation, P-A-K-E-N-H-A-M.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is that true, witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Because it's your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was my answer, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Bos, I'd like you to look at what's been put in front of you, marked as Exhibit 928C. Can you tell the Judges what that is.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: This is an envelope that contains a handwritten booklet, and that is the booklet that -- and the envelope that was given to me by my colleague Brett Pakenham.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since this is the first time that document has been in Court, could you just momentarily hold that up so the Judges are able to see the nature of the documented you're talk about. Could you open the cover, please, and just show what the pages look like.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: It looks like a normal diary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It doesn't matter. If you can just hold it up. Obviously the Chamber -- I know it's some distance, and the Chamber will of course have a chance to examine it. Now, let me -- my final question on the Rados diary, Ms. Bos, is: Were you able -- were you and a language assistant, a person who speak it is Bosnian Croat language -- excuse me, the Bosnian/Croat/Serb language that we refer to as B/C/S, were you able to review the original diary, that you have just shown to us, and handwritten copy, which was previously marked as, I believe, 928B, were you able to review those -- look at those documents in the last few days?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: We did. We looked at -- sorry, we looked at every page to see if there were differences between the pages in the original diary and the copy, what had been provided to us and what has been put into evidence. We checked it, if there had been something changed, and we couldn't find any changes. I also checked it, if there were pages lost, out, because it's numbered. I noticed there were five or six pages out, but the story continued from one page to the other page, so according to me and the language assistant, those pages were torn out before the diary was written, because it's a continuous story.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And other than that, were you able to as an investigator, did you find any other indications with the use of white-out, with the use of an eraser, scissors, did you see anything that indicated there had been any alteration made to the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that. There's been no foundation that this witness is an expert in documents or anything else. She's an investigator/police officer. She's no -- has no expertise for this question. There's lack of foundation, and I object. There's also been a lack of chain of custody on this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think this witness is an investigator. She's the first person to get hold of that document. Let us hear the impression of this witness. We know that the witness is not an expert in that specific field, but let's hear the impression of this witness. If you have some doubts, you may ask some questions in cross-examination. Witness, you may answer that question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to say that I'm not an expert, but the diary has lines. And if you look at it, if there has been something wiped out, you should be able to see that. We didn't see that, and we looked at the pages, all of them, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in terms of the follow-up on the objection just made by counsel, you said that another investigate named Mr. Pakenham brought the original diary back to The Hague from Bosnia, from the Mostar region, on approximately the 25th and 26th of September this year. Can you tell the Chamber whether that original diary has then been kept, secured from that time until the time that it has been produced in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we kept a record where the diary went as soon as it started to come into the -- into our building, and we have that on paper, where it was. So it hasn't gone anywhere else than amongst the investigators and the trial team.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, that concludes my questions on the diary. And I see it's 11.00. I could move to my next topic after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we now finally please have a look at this diary, since we weren't given an opportunity to review it before. My learned colleague did have this diary, but he kept silent about this both to the Chamber and to me, and he provided no copies. And now we heard when the diary came in, and you, Your Honours, ordered him to disclose anything related to that to us. Can we at least now have a look during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let me be clear on what your question is. You want to see the contents of the diary, or you want to see the diary itself? That's two different things. I think the Prosecution gave us kind of a photocopy on the contents of the diary rather than the diary itself. So you want to have a look at the diary itself or on the contents of the diary? You have to make it clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] Diary itself and contents, both. [Interpretation] We want to see that. And had we been given an opportunity in a timely fashion, maybe we could have studied the ink, the handwriting. Your Honours, please, this is the point we've reached. I have no further requests to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have no objections, of course, as long as Ms. Bos and a member of the registry staff could be present as long as the book is being examined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think that the diary should be examined by Defence counsel with the presence of somebody from the OTP as well as from the registrar. Well, we'll resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Scott, please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Bos, before we turn to the next topic, let me go back to the Office of the Prosecutor receiving the diary on approximately the 24th of September of this year. Can you tell the Judges, please, who did Mr. Pakenham receive the diary from.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: He received the diary from a FOSS official in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct, Ms. Bos, that FOSS, is a new combined, if you will, Croat/Muslim police or intelligence service formed in the last several months?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. At least that's what I have been told.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was what was previously called AID, or the Agency for Information and Documentation, was that agency, if you will, incorporated into and made part of the new Federation agency called FOSS?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's what I have been told, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it also correct that what had previously been the Bosnian Croat counterpart or similar police/intelligence agency, called SIS or sometimes SNS, that was also combined or incorporated into combined into FOSS?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's what I have been told, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, directing your attention forward to a different topic, Ms. Bos, focussing very specifically on the matter at hand. Is it correct that you were on mission in the Mostar region on approximately the 19th of November, 2001, when you received the request from the Office of the Prosecutor in The Hague to make efforts to locate a wooden rifle that might be related to this case?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. I was on mission at that time in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you just spend a moment or two telling the Judges in your own words the efforts that you made to locate such a rifle leading up to -- well, I'll let you go for some time, and then we'll take it then a step at a time further.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: On the 19th of November, while I was on mission in Mostar, I got a phone call from one of my colleagues with a request to look for one of the wooden rifles because one of the witnesses had testified about that. I made inquiries with -- as well as the local authorities in Mostar as some other people there. I had been told that the rifle had been seen in Jablanica some years ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this in -- in Jablanica. Was this in connection with something called "the museum"?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Yes, it was in Jablanica in a museum there. When I made inquiries, I had been told that it was not in Jablanica any more -- it was not in Jablanica there, and they would look around if they could find one for me. I myself went to the Mostar museum to see if it could have been there. I also went to the association for former camp prisoners in Mostar. I couldn't find it there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me just -- sorry to interrupt you, but just to prevent possibly naming the names of protected witnesses. Is it fair to say that you contacted a number of individuals in your efforts to locate a wooden rifle?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Please continue on.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: So on the 20th of November, I was produced a wooden rifle and a person. I met that person. I saw the rifle. And the person told me how he had gotten the wooden rifle in 1993, on 17th of September, while he had been serving along the front line defending East Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say you -- a rifle was produced to you on the 20th of November, 2001, can you tell the Judges, please, who introduced the rifle, to use your word -- to introduced the rifle to you.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: The witness and the rifle were introduced to me by the local authorities at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did those local authorities include what we've referred to in the courtroom as AID?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, can we go into private session, for, I think, one question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Bos, you said a moment ago that when you met this man with the rifle he told you that he had received it or initially obtained the rifle on the 17th of September, 1993. Could you just continue on with your answer about that.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. He told me that he had been defending the front line there, as I just said. He served along that front line from the health centre till the Santiceva Street. And on the 17th of September he was on duty between 11.00 and 14.00 in the afternoon. Around noon he saw a tank coming from the direction of Liska Street. Then after a while --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would object to this testimony. I believe it's outside the purview of this Trial Chamber's order. This witness was to testify and this witness has already testified that she received on rifle on the date previously given. This testimony is outside the scope and the purview of this Trial Chamber's order. It's unfortunate that the Prosecutor couldn't get this alleged soldier, individual who I won't name, to come to testify. I think it's highly improper to let this sort of testimony come in this Trial Chamber through this witness. This witness was to come and testify how she received this wooden rifle. She's already done that, and I think it's finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, first of all, we believe that the testimony of this witness is within the scope of the rebuttal proceedings, because she's going to tell us how she got that wooden rifle. Of course - of course - what she said was not her first-hand knowledge of how the wooden rifle fell into the hands of that person, but we all understand that the hearsay evidence is also allowed in the proceedings. When we evaluate this evidence, we will bear your objections in mind. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Bos, will you just continue on then with your answer. This man was stationed at the front line between approximately 11.00 in the morning and 2.00 in the afternoon on the 17th of September. You had started to talk about a tank. Can you please continue your testimony from there.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: At that time he was located opposite the health centre there. He saw the tank coming. And at that moment he didn't see soldiers there. But sometime later, shortly after, he all of a sudden saw four men, as I recall, four men already near the place where he was defending his part, and they were in HVO uniform -- at least the jackets were HVO uniform. They had a rifle with him. Just about when he was going to shoot, he noticed that the rifles were fake. As I remember, he only saw two rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- I'm sorry, no, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: So the -- then one of the prisoners said, "Don't shoot, because we are from your side." So they came in the building where he was defending and he remembered that from the four there were -- there was one prisoner what was a bit more heavy weight than the others. The others were thinner. He also remembers that he received cigarettes from one of them. And as he said, from that one, the one that was more heavy weight. And he remembers that he asked if he could get that wooden rifle from that man and he received that and he kept it. He took the rifle home with him and never gave it to someone else or modified it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on that day - we're now talk again -- we're still on the 20th of November, 2001 -- did you actually obtain possession of the rifle at that time, that is, obtain the rifle and bring it back to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because when I asked him if I could take the rifle with me, he said, "No -- yes, you can but you have to pay me 300 Deutschmarks for that, because I need the money. One of my children is sick and he needs an operation." I told him that the Tribunal was not going to pay for such a thing, but he insisted, and I agreed with him that he should come back the next morning. I would discussion this with my chiefs and would go back to him the next morning, the following morning. He agreed on that. He left the rifle behind. I discussed it with the chief of investigations in the Tribunal, and it was confirmed that we are not paying for that. So I made photos that evening, that late afternoon, and the next morning I was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. Forgive me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what's been marked as Exhibit P963. Mr. President, Your Honours, copies of these -- colour copies of those -- those are the photographs, nine photos of the wooden rifle, colour copies are provided in the binders that have been distributed to the Chamber. Perhaps the usher could -- the assistant -- we could use one of the binders, if it's easier -- one of the bundles that have been prepared for witnesses and simply put those on the ELMO, if there is one. Actually, if I might assist. Madam Registrar, I don't think it's necessary. I think the -- I think that the Judges have those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, Ms. Bos, taking photographs as you just said on the evening or approximately the evening of the 20th of November, 2001?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I made those photos, and I took those photos with me back to The Hague. And as far as I know, those photos have been submitted to the Court and the Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Ms. Bos, we've now located a copy of those for purposes of the witness stand. If those could -- if you could just briefly look at those just so you can verify that those are the photographs that you took at that time.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I took that photo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we're not going to go -- can you just look physically, just leaf through the photographs and confirm that those are the photographs you took. We're not going to go through each one.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I can confirm they took all these photos and I also made the measure, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's the one other photo that I was going to ask you about. Is there one other photo in that bundle that has measurements?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: There is one photo amongst them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
