utterances.text: Could that please be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you just confirm, Ms. Bos, that you're the one who made the measurements that have been placed on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I can confirm that, sir. I made those measures and I wrote them down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's the -- I have no more questions about the photographs. You said that you had made arrangements with this man to meet him again the next day. Did you?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I did, sir. And -- but he didn't turn up the next morning. And I was told that he -- they couldn't find him. And as I had arranged that I would travel back to Sarajevo that day, I had to leave and couldn't wait for him. So actually, I proposed that I would take the rifle, because it was obvious the man was not coming and most probably didn't care about it any more. But that was strongly rejected by the official of at that time AID. The man had asked money for it and wanted to be paid for it and I hadn't paid him. So I left the rifle behind to have it given back to the man and I left Sarajevo -- left Mostar for Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you continue after that -- after the completion of that mission and your return to The Hague, did you engage in further efforts between the end of November and January of this year, 2002, to locate -- either to locate a rifle or indeed to deal with this man again about that rifle?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. About Jablanica museum, I had heard that it was not open and I had also spoken to someone who had spoken with a caretaker there who hadn't heard about it or who didn't know about it. On my next mission in January, I planned to see the man from the wooden rifle again to make another effort to bring the rifle with me without paying, which I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the result of your meeting with this man, the same man that you'd met on the 20th of November? What was the outcome of that meeting on that day?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I met him on the 19th of January on the street, which was accidentally. I asked if he -- if he could speak again. He agreed on that, but it was a bit later that day. I went to his house, and I asked him again if I could get the rifle without paying and told him that we need it. He wanted to think about it and told me to come back two days later, which I did. So on the 21st of January, I returned to his house and there was no -- I have to tell that there was no interference of any other official in this, also not on the 19th of January, when I met him. So I went back to his house and he was prepared to hand me over the rifle but he told me that if we had used it, if he could have it back because it had some emotional value to him. I told him that I would discuss that. He didn't want to give a signed statement or testify because of security reasons, and he didn't want to be involved in that because he had gone through a lot of -- a lot of bad things during the war and he didn't want to go over that any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask -- I'm sorry. Let me just ask you: The rifle, then, that you saw, that he produced to you on approximately the 21st of January, did you confirm to the Judges, was that the same rifle that you had seen on the 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: When he handed over to me the rifle on the 21st of November, I looked at it and I saw it was the same rifle I had seen on the 20th of November and which I had photographed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Ms. Bos, I think you may have just misspoke. But you say when he handed the rifle to you -- if you look at the transcript -- on the 21st of November. Did you mean to say the 21st of January?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Sorry. It must have been the 21st of January. He handed it over to me, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me just clarify the record. When you received the rifle from the man on the 21st of January, was it the same rifle that you had seen in November?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: It was the same rifle I had seen in November, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: With the usher's assistance, can we show this, please, to -- what's been marked as Exhibit 962 to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Bos, examining before you what's been marked as Exhibit 962, can you tell the Judges what that is.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: This is the so-called wooden rifle, what I received from that witness on the 21st of January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I only have, I believe, two remaining questions for you. The photographs -- directing your attention back to the photographs. You need not have the photographs. But when you retained these photographs earlier, did you have occasion to show these -- those photographs to a man who is identified -- and I will ask you not to use any names. But did you show the photographs to a man known in this courtroom as Witness PP?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Yes. I was able to do so, because that witness was still here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: In The Hague, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that man able to give you any information about the rifle shown in those photographs that have been marked as Exhibit 963?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I showed him the photos, and he identified the rifle as the rifle he had been carrying -- a very, very similar rifle as he had been carrying on the 17th of September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you obtained -- physically obtained the rifle that you have in front of you now on the witness stand, were you able to physically show that rifle to the man known as Witness PP?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: When I returned back in Sarajevo and I had the rifle with me, I called the witness, I showed him the rifle, and he identified the rifle as the rifle he had been carrying on the 17th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally, Ms. Bos, carry that rifle back to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I personally took it with me and brought it in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges where that rifle, other than having it in the courtroom -- where that rifle has been since brining it back to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: When I brought it back -- I brought it to our evidence unit, where it was stored.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my final question is: Is it correct that on -- I believe it was Friday last week that you met with Mr. Par, Mr. Seric, and showed them -- and had a chance to meet with them concerning that rifle.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's correct. I showed the rifle to them here in the office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Bos. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination? Yes, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have agreed that we will be the first ones to carry out our cross-examination, but Mr. Krsnik will explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the break that we are headed for, we would like to see this concoction that we have received today. And if nothing else, we would like to compare the original with the copies in order to be able to carry out -- to conduct my cross-examination. That's why I asked my colleague Par to start cross-examining and allow me to prepare myself. If I can't do that during the lunch break, I will ask you to give me the permission to continue with my cross-examination tomorrow, because I really do need the time to compare the original with the copies of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I hope you could do it during the lunch break, because, you know, we are really racing against the time. Mr. Par, are you ready to do your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I'm ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, I saw that first row is always empty. Why don't you take that one. Yes. Cross-examined by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Ms. Bos. I am Zelimir Par. We've had opportunity to meet, and I represent Vinko Martinovic before this Tribunal. Before we start the cross-examination, I would like to tell you that there are two statements the Defence wishes to make in relation to your testimony. The first one being: We believe that the wooden rifle that you have testified about today is an important -- is a false piece of evidence and that it was planted. Our second statement is: We believe your testimony related to this wooden rifle is aimed at convincing the Chamber that it is indeed an authentic piece of evidence and not a false piece of evidence. It is on the basis of these two statements by the Defence that I will ask you several questions. Mrs. Bos, do you believe that this wooden rifle that you have testified about was planted, to you to lead you to believe that it was a rifle that was used in some sort of military operation on the 17th of September, 1993 in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no reason to believe that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, witness, would you please repeat your answer. I don't think --

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have understood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the response of the witness, I would like to say that I haven't understood Mr. Par's question. Can Mr. Par please repeat the question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. My question was the following: Does the witness believe that this rifle was planted?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I have no reason to believe this, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Bos, do you rule out the possibility that this rifle was planted?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I object to that, Your Honour. Ruling out all possibilities I think is an unfair question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, you have to -- you have to rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I also think that it's inappropriate for the Prosecution to offer answers that the witness is supposed to provide. I will return to this matter through some other questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Bos, your testimony before this court, is the aim of this testimony to prove to us that this is indeed an authentic piece of evidence?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the aim, as far as I believe, is to present the Court with evidence on the incident, what happened on the 17th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to take my place just next to my learned colleague Par, Mr. President, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that I should be able to participate should the need arise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: While Mr. Seric is doing that, Your Honour, that last answer this witness made went directly to the objection I made ten minutes ago which you overruled. This witness is only here to testify how she received this piece of evidence. And now she's answered she believes her aim is to present evidence on the incident of the 17th of September, which is not within the scope of the rebuttal. I want to make the record clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you know, Mr. Meek, the witness is not as trained a legal professional as us. She does not know the exact areas that she is going to testify. Judging from her answer, I think it's within the scope of the rebuttal proceedings. Anyway, Mr. Par, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us start with the following, Mrs. Bos, our thesis that this piece of evidence was planted. Could you please tell us, what was the first time that you saw this rifle? Can you repeat the date, please.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: The first time I saw the rifle was on the 20th of November, 2001, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us again, who was the person who showed you the rifle for the first time.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: The rifle was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you are going to mention some names, we have to go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We would request that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How, then, did this member of the AID happen to be in your office? Did you have an appointment? Did he let you know before about being in possession of this rifle? How did the meeting between the two of you in that office come about?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: As I've already said before, when I got the request to look for that rifle, I discussed it with local authorities, with this member of the AID and some other people. And when I discussed it, he said well, he would look around if he could find such a rifle, if it was still in Mostar. I was working in that office anyway, so he came up during the morning. I think it was end of the morning with that rifle. He knew I was in that office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please clarify this term for us "local authorities." You say, "I worked with local authorities." Are we talking about the police forces? Are we talk about the AID or some other local authorities?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I'm talking about the AID, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The point we're about to reach is the point where we should name the person the rifle belonged to;, however one wishes to refer to him. How did he get there to your meeting point, this office? Was he brought there by this member of the AID?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: He was brought by a member of the AID, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just another question concerning this meeting: Were you too -- did you too -- did you invite them to this meeting, or did they just say themselves, "We'll be there with the rifle tomorrow at some point"? Who initiated this meeting?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Well, we didn't initiate a meeting. I am working in that office anyway. So if they bring something or there is something, they come to that office. They know where they can find me. So we did not arrange anything to say well, as far as I remember, I'm going to bring you a rifle. It was just brought to me there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this witness - let's call him Witness AK, for example, is here. What did he tell you? Did you ask him who the rifle belonged to? Who was the person who interviewed him, you, the AID member?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: To clarify, sir, when I interview witnesses there's never someone from the AID present. So as soon as he came in the office, the AID official left and I was the one who asked the witness the questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you ask him about who the rifle belonged to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you obtain an answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, my apology to counsel. I appreciate that counsel is trying to protect the identity of this man. This is not a complaint. However, we should probably not use AK, because that's a pseudonym that's been assigned to another witness. Perhaps we can assign a new pseudonym to this person, if that's the easiest thing to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. What's your suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Or the man. I mean, I think we're only talking -- we're only talking about the man who came to the office on that day. But however the Chamber wishes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My learned colleague has just informed me that man is not a witness, has refused to be a witness, and there are no protective measures involved. He only asked not to have his name mentioned, and we'll respect that. We'll comply with that. We can call him "Person X," or whichever way you like. I really don't want to hurt his priorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik. I thought this matter has been settled by both parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. No. I'm confused here. I am not an expert on procedure. That's why I always closely observe the way the Statute is applied. But I have familiarised myself with it. But can someone please tell me, why should there be any protective measures for a person who is not at all a witness before this Court. Why should this person be protected in that way? Is this in any of the regulations and provisions of the Statute? Why do we approve this course of action? We don't know who the person is and he's never likely to appear before this court. So how do we get to protect him and on the basis of what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I think you are talking about a theoretical matter. And in this case, both parties agreed we call this person "Person X," and the parties -- and this Trial Chamber has no objections about it. If you want to know some theoretical issues, we could discuss it at another time. Now we have a witness here doing her testimony. Let us move on because we are really behind the schedule. Mr. Par, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did this Person X tell you that the rifle belonged to him in the interview you had?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say that this rifle had once been in a museum somewhere?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: No, sir. As I already said, he told me that he had taken it home after he had obtained it from the Muslim prisoner on the 17th of September, took it home, and it didn't go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the information you obtained from that person during that interview. My question is: You as an investigator - that's based on the information you obtained from Person X - did you really ascertain that this was indeed a rifle that was used during that operation? Was this the information you used to ascertain that this rifle was related to the events that transpired on the 17th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: He told me how he had received the rifle, and that's the information I gave you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: Is this the information that you used as an investigator and then forwarded your conclusions to your superior that this rifle was related to events on the 17th of September, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: It was this information and the information from the Witness PP which had recognised the rifle on the photos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But back then you were not in a position to discuss any photographs or to know anything about Witness PP. So let us please just follow the chronology of events. The answer you have just provided creates a nexus between two different things, a nexus which back at that point had not existed, so please let us just try to follow the chronology. However, let us return to the same information in the light of those witnesses who claimed they'd seen the rifle. You have stated that the first time you saw the rifle was on the 20th of November, 2001. Immediately before that Witness OO testified that such a rifle indeed existed but refused to give away its precise location. Were you aware of this, that this was actually stated in this courtroom just prior to the time you found the rifle?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I was informed that Witness OO had given a statement and had said that he had -- as I recall, that he had seen it in the museum in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was immediately before the time you were to see this rifle for the first time. That was just before.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Bos, is it correct that prior to that you had spent years investigating this case and you'd never heard of the existence of such a rifle, although you had talked to a large number of witnesses connected with the possible existence of this rifle. But am I correct in saying in you'd never heard of the existence of this rifle before?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I'd never heard of the existence of the rifle before, that it still existed. And I only started this investigation in June 2001.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you surprised that information on this rifle should emerge at such a late date, even if -- given that you had studied and investigated the case for quite some time by that point? Were you surprised?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: In a way I was surprised. I had not expected it, actually. And I think I have to correct me [sic]. I started this investigation in 2000, to work on this investigation. I think it was in June 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, were you surprised how it came about that only several days after this information was obtained suddenly the rifle is there in the possession of a man we referred to as Person X? You had been investigating the case for quite some time. Suddenly this information comes up in court and in several days the rifle emerges. Didn't that seem surprising since you had spent some time investigating the case and the possibility was never spoken of that the rifle could be found? Now, weren't you surprised to suddenly find this very rifle in the possession of Person X?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Well, given the fact that Person X kept it at home, it might not be known to everybody that the rifle still existed. And I have to admit that I do not know exactly how much effort we have put in to see if the rifle still existed. I think we were of the impression that the rifles were not there any more, after such a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us please go back to the issue that my learned colleague Scott had objected, but in a different way now. Can you completely rule out the possibility that under all these circumstances someone may have - and I am referring here most of all to the AID, who followed closely witness testimonies and who cooperated with you and they did have information regarding the type of rifle you were looking for - so can you completely rule out the possibility that within that very short space of time the AID made sure that just such a rifle was made, manufactured, and forwarded to you in order to corroborate evidence given by previous witnesses? Can you completely rule out such a possibility?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I can only say that I saw the rifle for the first time on the 20th of November. I was not there when Mr. X received it. I was not there all the time when he kept it in his house. But as you are referring to this, if this was a plan from the AID, why didn't they produce it earlier and why didn't they produce another witness with it, a witness who was willing to testify about it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can tell you what we believe: That they did it at just the point when it was necessary for them, because no witness had ever referred to such a wooden rifle before. But sudden through as soon as a witness came up with a wooden rival, they did it, just at the right time and on the first occasion they needed to. However, let us proceed. Let's stick to this hypothesis that the wooden rifle had been planted by AID members. But let's try to see the situation through the eyes of our Person X. Can you please tell us without saying the person's name or relating any information that might give away the person's identity, but still can you tell us something about that man, what you know about him, without disclosing his identity. And should that occur, we'll ask the Court to please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's what I -- Mr. President, that's what I'm asking, that we go into private session, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I saw his identity card.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us then: When was it that you saw the ID card? When?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: On the 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe to us the way you identified that person.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I saw his identity card. He gave me his name. And the name on that identity card was the same as the name he gave me. And of course, there was a photo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Bos, I am not letting you off the hook that easily. I don't believe that you saw the ID card, and that's why I am going to insist on every detail, on what occasion did you see the ID card? Tell me when, what exchange of information passed between the two of you, who said what to whom. Exact details I want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I -- this has been answered now several times. I don't think there's any anything unequivocal at all. An investigator has testified that she saw the ID card on the 20th of November. She saw it, she gave the information, his citizenship, name, the photo. I object. It's already been answered, clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Also Mr. Par is actually accusing this witness of giving perjury. And as far as I can see, all the questions are directed at the identification or bona fides of the person furnishing the rifle rather than addressing any questions at all to the rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I -- Judge Clark, you're absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I honestly don't know where you're going, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I also say the same. I didn't -- I share that. I think if counsel -- I understand his desire to create -- to conduct a full cross-examination, but I would just caution counsel. If he's attacking the bona fides of this witness, a professional investigator, then I hope he has some specific basis to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my learned friend, I'm asking the witness about the identification of a person who is the key witness, key person to present the piece of evidence on which the witness that is now before us is testifying. My allegation, although I respect the witness as a professional investigator, my allegation is that the piece of evidence has been passed on her, that the person was -- is false. This Person X, whose name we are not allowed to pronounce in this courtroom, may be a false person. Maybe that person doesn't exist. Maybe that is another official of the AID. Maybe it was just a local criminal who was brought in to show the rifle, and I believe it is my right to establish the identity of that person. That's number one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Par, you're perfectly entitled to do that. But what you are not entitled to do, unless you have very good grounds for doing so, is to accuse a witness of lying to this Court. And not an ordinary witness. This is a professional member of the OTP. You have accused this witness of lying. Now, lay the foundation for that. I can understand, Mr. Par, if you say that you don't accept the bona fides of the witness who introduced the so-called gun. You're perfectly entitled to do that. But to say to this witness who has told you, "I saw the ID," to say, "I don't believe you saw it and I'm not going to let you off the hook," now, I have to have grounds for saying that. She may have seen a false ID, did you she says that she saw an ID? It had the man's name on it and a photograph. Now, do you have any foundation for saying this witness has told the Court an untruth? This is between Mr. Par and the Court, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'll wait until you are finished then, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Clark, this is exactly what I was going to say as my second remark. This witness here has not given us the adequate information to be able -- for us to be able to identify this person. So this is the information that could not corroborate the identity of that person. Secondly, in none of the statements by this witness there are identification information for that person. Thirdly, I asked the witness whether she identified the person, whether she inspected any identification documents. After a long time she decided to say that she did see the ID and she insists on that. Why do I dare say that I doubt, that I have my reservations about that, and that I want to verify that information? I believe that the veracity of the testimony before this and any other tribunal is proven by the circumstances of the event. I cannot take it for granted when a witness said, "I saw an ID card." It is my right to establish the circumstances of the event, when that took place. So when she saw it, how she saw it, and based on that it is my right to establish whether the witness is telling the truth. I believe that this is the way all the courts all over the world work. Whether my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Par, can I -- forgive -- you're missing my point. You're entitled to cross-examine on credibility and relevance. That is absolutely your right and indeed it's your duty. But what you are not allowed to do is to say to a witness that you are telling lies unless you have foundation for that. Now, it was translated on the monitor in front of me as you saying "I do not believe that you, Ms. Bos, saw the ID card." Ms. Bos said she saw the ID card. Now, you tell this Court why you said to this witness that you do not believe she's telling the truth. Now, address your remarks to that. Do you want to withdraw that remark, or do you want to now furnish us with the foundation for why you said it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you will allow me, I will continue cross-examining about the circumstances. I already put it to our colleague from the Prosecutor's Office, and I told you why I did not believe it and I repeat why I don't believe it and why I put it to the witness that I didn't believe it. I respect the witness as a professional affiliated with the Prosecutor's Office, as a person with a certain experience in investigations and who will understand why I am asking certain questions. But if you want me to withdraw this question, I believe I shouldn't skip any further questions about the circumstances of the identification and I hope you will allow me to proceed questioning this witness along these lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Par, I want you to be absolutely clear. You are well within your rights to cross-examine this witness as efficiently and as harshly as you want. You're certainly entitled to do that. But what I'm saying is you are not entitled to say that what she says she did was a lie. Now, if you want to withdraw -- there may be, and it's happened before, a problem about translation. This witness says she saw an ID. It may well be that you believe it was a false ID. But you questioned the integrity of this witness when she said, "I saw the ID," and you said you don't believe you saw it. Do you want to withdraw that remark and then we can move on?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to continue, and therefore I would like -- I can withdraw that remark, but I would like to continue asking the questions along this same line. But if the witness is offended by my line of questioning, then I will withdraw my thoughts entirely and I will rephrase all of my future questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Ms. Bos, let's forget my allegation and let's move on to talk about the identification of this person whom we've referred to as Citizen X. Can you please tell us, when did he show you his ID card? How did that happen? How did that come about?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: He showed me the ID card on the 20th of November, when I saw him. And I asked his ID card, so he gave it to me. And I looked at it. It was the same name he gave me. Date of birth, I can't recall that now. Photo on it. That was a normal Bosnian-Herzegovinan ID card.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on that ID card, did you make a note of any of the data from that ID card? Did you copy any of the information anywhere?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I didn't make any notes of that identity card, and I also didn't copy it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you conduct an interview with other witnesses, is that your normal practice when you try to establish their identity?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: The normal practice, that you look at the identity card, check, and then you give it back to the witness. We are not in a position to make quickly a copy of an identity card.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Term us please once again if you can remember, what did that ID card look like? Was it old, worn out? Was it new? What was the photo like? Was it a black-and-white photo? Was it a colour photo? Can you remember what the ID card looked like?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: The ID card was plastified [sic]. I didn't have the impression that it was worn out, but I just have to recall my memory. It was not worn out, as I can remember, and it was visible to me who he was. The photo was visible to me. As I already said, it was yellowish-coloured. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't make a note of any of the information that you found on the ID card. There's no trace, a written trace of any of that information, so you did not make a note of the fact that you identified the person based on the ID furnished to you.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: No, sir, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on. The Citizen X produced his ID card. He talks to you. He provides you with certain information. My question to you is the following: Do you know, Ms. Bos, whether that Person X, during 1993, was a member of the BH Army? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. He told me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in any way in the position to check that information; namely, that he was a member of the BH Army? Did you check his military ID by any chance?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I didn't check his military identity card. But I was also told by the AID official that he was a former ABiH soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I asked you whether the AID official told you anything about that person, you told me that he didn't say anything about that he was a member of the BH Army. Okay. So can we agree that the information that I have presented before this Chamber today - and that is that the Person X was a member of the BH Army - was the information that you obtained only from the official of the AID and from that person himself, and that is that this is your only basis for your allegation that he was a member of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct. I got to know he was in the army from the AID person later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know, Ms. Bos, where this Person X was on the 17th of September, 1993? Do you know that? And if you do, how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: As I told before, Mr. X told me that on the 17th of September he was on duty between 11.00 and 2.00, as I recall, and he was doing his duty in the building opposite the health centre, the ruins, and he was actually, as I remember, in the basement defending East Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my question was asked in order to find out whether you have any other information as to his whereabouts on the 17th of September, 1993 but his own statement; in other words, whether you checked the credibility of the story told to you by that person X, as to his whereabouts on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I didn't check that, sir. He was not willing to testify. He was not willing to give a signed statement. And there was not information to check it at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Bos, was that the reason perhaps -- wasn't that a good enough reason for you to check the information? Wasn't the fact that he didn't want to issue an official statement, that he didn't want to have his name Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. ever mentioned, that he didn't want to tell you the names of his comrades, that he didn't know who gave him the rifle, weren't these good enough reasons for you as an investigator to verify all that information before you told your colleagues in the Prosecutor's Office that this was the person who was holding that rifle on the Bulevar on that day? Weren't these good enough reasons for you to verify all that, to double-check the information?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: At that moment I didn't check it. I have interviewed more witnesses than this witness, and it happened before that witnesses are hesitant to say certain things because of security reasons or reasons that they want to go -- they don't want us to bother people. And for this witness I didn't -- before I went back to The Hague, I didn't check. Only I liaised with an AID official who confirmed to me that he was a former ABiH soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it ever happen to you that other witnesses ever told you, I'm going to give you this piece of evidence but I want 300 German marks in return? Is that something that often happened, and wouldn't that be a good enough reason for an investigator to check the information and to see how come that person all of a sudden appears out of the blue skies, asks for money without giving any information in return? So as an investigator, did you have any reasons to verify the circumstances of the appearance of that witness? So wasn't that something that made you think twice in the presence of such evidence?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: First of all, sir, I never -- it never happened to me that a witness was asking money. Secondly, I know that the economic circumstances in this country are very bad. Not that I agree that people should ask money for certain things, but he asked me for money, and I couldn't give it to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But finally you did give him the money. Am I right in thinking that? Did I understand that well, that the Prosecutor's Office eventually did pay? If not, then I made a mistake. How -- since none of us are clear on that, can you please tell me whether the payment was subsequently approved by this Tribunal by the Prosecutor's Office. Was that Person X ever paid the money that he asked for?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: As I remember, I think I just told sometime ago that I obtained the rifle without paying for it, because when I went back to him in January I told him I couldn't pay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need another minute, another question, please, and I will wind up before the break, if you will allow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to this subject, I would like to come to some conclusions. You told me you didn't verify -- my repeated question was whether you had any reasons to verify. Now, my question to you is: Was the only thing important to you at the time, Ms. Bos, was to bring to the Prosecutor's Office a wooden rifle of any kind so as to make sure that the Prosecutor's witness didn't give a false testimony? Wasn't maybe that the reason why you didn't spend too much time to verify the identity of the person? Maybe it was more important for you to bring any sort of evidence to your colleagues. And was that the reason why you didn't do all the checking and double-checking of the identity of the person?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Sir, it was important for me that with the rifle I would also get the witness. But if the witness says, "I do not want to give a statement. I do not want to testify," I can only bring the rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have finished, and we can now have the break if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, when and how can we get hold of this diary, the so-called diary? Where and how can we see, read, peruse the diary? Can you please instruct me as to where I should go to peruse the so-called diary? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think, first of all, I have to go to Madam Registrar, because that diary is in her possession. And we also want the presence of the -- somebody from the OTP. I hope you could do that during the lunch break. I understand that you all know the contents already. You just want to know the diary itself, the typing, the -- the paper, you know, the cover, you know, all those matters. Well, we'll resume at 2.30 this afternoon. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1 1.03 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, did you finish your cross-examination or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to turn to a different area now. In the first part of my cross-examination, I was talking about the source. And now I would like to turn to the issue of the identification of this rifle. I don't think that should take too long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Bos, as I have just told the Court, I would like us to talk a little about how this unverified story told by Person X and the wooden rifle tried to be somehow fitted into the needs of the Prosecution concerning their evidence. So my first question will be: Is it true that you showed photographs of this rifle to Witnesses OO and PP who testified before this Court that they had held just such a rifle in their own hands? Were you the one who had shown them the photographs?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. I showed the photographs to Witness PP, and my colleague shows the photographs to Witness OO, but I was also present when that happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, is it true that on that particular occasion, judging by looking at the photographs, Witness OO said in a very decided manner that that was not the rifle he had and that he gave all the differences between the rifle in the photograph and the rifle that he had purportedly held in his own hands? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, sir. He mentioned the differences, but he also mentions that one particular thing was the same as this rifle. That was the thick -- it was as thin as the same rifle he saw on the photo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he -- was he really in a position to judge about how thick the rifle was on the basis of a two-dimensional photograph?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I made a photo standing up showing how thin it was with a person next to it, so a little bit of that -- I mean, if you would take that in consideration, I think you can a bit measure how thin it was or how thick it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question, Mrs. Bos, was more specifically: On that occasion, did the witness not say, very decidedly, "This is not the rifle that I had"?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Bos, isn't it true that on that same occasion Witness PP was not able to confirm that that wooden rifle shown in the photograph was indeed the same rifle that he had purportedly held in his hands? Isn't it true that he also enumerated a number of differences between the two rifles and that he merely stated that the rifle in the photograph merely looked very much like the one that he had had? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not correct that both witnesses, Witness OO and Witness PP, claimed that their wooden rifle was black?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I do remember that Witness PP said that. But from a photo it was difficult to judge for him. But he indeed said it was black.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just trying to be as accurate as I can. I'm not asking about the colour of the rifle in the photograph but whether the two witnesses in their testimony, after enumerating the differences, both confirmed that the rifle they were talking about was indeed painted black. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: At this moment I can only remember that Witness PP said that, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I please remind you on the basis of the statements that you took.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't think it's fair for this to be a memory test. It's obvious now that for some minutes counsel is questioning the witness based on prior statements and I think it's only fair to put the statements in front of her so she can consult them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Par, if you want to use that previous statement, you'd better furnish that statement to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour. I was just about to show the witness her statement to remind her of the circumstances. I think that is a widely accepted method and one permitted by this Court. Could the usher please help me with this and give the English version of the statement of Witness OO, dated the 22nd of November, 2001. And here I can see that the witness was interviewed by Mr. Romeau Ventura. So may the witness please have a look to verify this issue of the colour of the wooden rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's in the last part of the statement, where the witness says that he has looked carefully at the photographs and then goes on to enumerate the differences. So I think the first sentence of that particular passage is "I am able to point out the differences that I have ascertained exist between the two rifles, the one that I used was painted black. The one I can see in the photograph is not painted black. Probably the image is dark, but it doesn't look like real colour to me." So can you please look through the statement and find that sentence. That's what I will base my question on. I'm going to ask you whether you are aware of the fact that Witness OO also said that the wooden rifle was painted black.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I'm look at the statement, sir. And as I already said, I only interviewed Witness PP, not Witness OO, although I was present when he looked at the photo. I see it's in the statement, so yeah, I'm aware of it. I didn't know it any more on top of my head because I didn't take that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Par. We were wondering if we could have a copy of that statement so we could look at it while you're referring to it. Would it be possible? Without delaying the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't really expect that the witness would challenge this quote, so I don't have any extra copies. But my proposal is -- this is the last page of the statement, so may it please be put on the ELMO, displayed there. It's only about a couple of sentences. So we can put it on the ELMO for everyone to see. Could the usher please put the statement, the last page of the statement on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The statement, I hope, doesn't identify Witness X, does it, or Mr. X?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The page that I'd like to have on the ELMO does not, I think, contain the person's name. I'm checking the Croatian version now. There is no name on that particular page. So may the witness please have a look and see if there is a name on that page of the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is the name of the witness, the protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is none here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because there is no signature on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we put only this half of the page on the ELMO without the signature, we won't be able to see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can't see it on our screens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of this first sentence in the second passage, where it reads "I can tell the differences found on the two of them. The one that I used was painted black." So can we agree that Witness OO indeed also claimed that it was a rifle, a black rifle, a rifle painted black? Can you please answer that question?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We shall no longer require this document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, no objection. But I think it's very clear. And I assume counsel is not going back and force intentionally. But when Witness OO says it's not -- it wasn't his rifle, he's not talking about -- he's talking about the rifle he carried. We have to be very clear which rifle these witnesses are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, we all understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, it was confusing to me until just now with all these statements, which -- the statement of which witness, about whose rifle we were talking about. If -- sorry, if everyone understands that, fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I clarify that. Are we talking now about Witness OO? Are we going to hear what Witness PP said?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours -- and if the witness could just please follow what I'm talking about so she can react if I have misinterpreted anything. My question to the witness was: "Is it true that both Witness OO and Witness PP, when photographs of these rifles were shown to them, claimed that the rifle which they had allegedly held in their own hands was black?" The witness's answer was that she remembers that Witness PP had indeed said that the rifle he had allegedly held in his own hands was black. However, the witness added that she couldn't remember whether Witness OO claimed the same thing. Following that, I showed our witness here the statement taken from the Witness OO after the photograph had been shown to him in order to ascertain what exactly the witness said about the rifle on that occasion. Now the witness has agreed that Witness OO also claimed that the rifle he had allegedly had on the 17th of September, 1993, was indeed painted black. So that, I think, explains it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Bos, is it true that the rifle we saw today, the way you stated it, is brown and you, too, have ascertained this fact in your own report?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: The rifle at the moment is brownish. But if you have a good look at it, you can see there are some black faded on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Counsel, I apologise for interrupting you. But I think it's only fair that the rifle -- that the witness should have the rifle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sure. Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, please, I am not sure who's the one who decides what should be done or what should not be done during my cross-examination. My learned friend Scott with no permission from the Chamber presents evidence to the witness who is currently being cross-examined by me, while I think in that case I should just leave the floor to him and allow him to finish my cross-examination, because this seems quite pointless.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The witness has answered the question. She said that "The rifle at the moment is brownish. But if you have a good look at it, you can see there are some black faded on it." The witness has already answered that question already. Then the Prosecutor asked to show this rifle to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise. Counsel -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, counsel is partly right. And I apologise. When we left the -- when we left before the break, the rifle was on the witness stand but for the break, if this testimony had continued, the rifle would have remained on the witness stand. And I just assumed that it was still available to the witness. And if I acted too quickly, I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. That's true. You may proceed, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I cannot by any means accept this argument, this case by the Prosecutor. Rifle or no rifle we started the examination the way we did, and no one here was authorised by the Chamber to have the rifle presented to the witness. I don't mind. Of course, we can show the witness the rifle. And the Prosecutor too can show the rifle to the witness in their additional questions. I was just talk about what exactly the witness had stated in her own report, because her words were that the rifle was brown. I wanted to draw attention again to her own report and then that's what our common sense tells us. Here is the rifle. Here is the colour. We all have healthy eyes and we can all judge for ourselves concerning the colour of the rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So please, witness, answer any way which you like, what is the colour of this rifle? You can have a careful look now and tell us what you think. After that, I would like the usher, please, to show the rifle around the courtroom so that everyone can see for themselves, both the brown colour and the black spots. So please, witness, can you have a look at the rifle and tell us what colour you think it is.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: At the moment, as I see it now, the colour is brownish and has some black spots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do you see these black spots? Which part of the rifle?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: In here and in here, in here. Here it is more dark, blackish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you believe that this is a painted rifle, or do you think that's just the natural colour of old wood?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I don't think I can answer that question. I'm not an expert on this, and I wouldn't like to give the wrong answer on that, so I'll leave that to others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the rifle around, first of all to the Chamber and then also to the other interested parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Usher, Mr. Par, does your client want to have a look at it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My client does not have a particular wish to look at this rifle, because he thinks this is planted evidence. That's what he told me. As we were looking at the rifle, my learned colleague Meek told me that the answer by the witness was not recorded in the transcript. The question was whether Witness OO, after inspecting the photograph, said "I can say in a decided manner that the rifle shown in the photograph is not the rifle that I had had on the 17th of September," whereupon the witness replied that "that was indeed the conclusion of the witness." I'm only repeating this for the sake of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let us please now return to the issues we discussed before my learned friend Scott gave us the rifle. We were talking about the following: Witness OO stated decidedly that it was not the rifle he had used. Witness PP said that it only resembled the other rifle. And both of the witnesses actually claimed with certainty that the rifle they'd used was black. Now, my question to you is: After this photo identification of the rifle, the Prosecution was not really happy with the reliability of that piece of evidence. And then a new task was assigned to you. You were to continue your work on trying to prove that this rifle really went back to the events on the 17th of September, 1993. Is that true, that you really were assigned such a task, that is, to connect this rifle to the events of the 17th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I understand that counsel has the right to put his case. But when it's continually put in the -- of challenging the integrity and ethics of the Prosecution team, I have a serious problem with that. He is suggesting that it was the deliberate plan of the Prosecution team to find evidence and only evidence that supported its case and that an investigator was put in the field specifically for that purpose. Now, again, I understand that he can put the case -- we understand that they think this is a fabricated rifle. We all understand that. But I object to the way the questions are being put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, you may rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Bos, please, what sort of assignment were you given after the inspection of the photographs? Why did you have to return to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: To be very precise, sir, it was my own proposal to go back and try again with the witness to get the rifle, because I knew that -- I mean, I could go back and convince him that I could get it, I would do that. Although, the witness had already said that he didn't want to give it, only for money, and he didn't want to give a statement, I wanted to give it another try and so it was assigned to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why if it was never confirmed in the first place that the rifle had anything to do with the witnesses, at least not up to that moment, was that one of your plans to work on that? What did you need the rifle for if there had never been any confirmation in the first place that that indeed was the rifle everyone was talking about?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Witness PP said when he saw the photos that this could very well be the rifle. So if I was able to obtain the rifle, I could show it to him, the rifle. So he might be -- have a better chance to recognise it or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Bos, so we have to be precise here and go back to PP's statement, who didn't say that it was exactly that rifle but that it was similar to the one he had. So I don't want to show you the statement again, but this is what he said, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That is correct. But I saw him watching the photo, and I saw that it was not so very easy to judge the rifle from the photo. And he also said that. But in the end, he said that it was very much like the rifle he had been carrying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement it says it was "similar," not "very similar," so that was the reason why you went back to Mostar in order to try and talk again with PP about the rifle. Was that the underlying cause about your return to Mostar? Is it fair for me to understand it that way?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: No, sir. I didn't go back to Mostar for that only assignment. I had other assignments. And I took this assignment with me also. I didn't go for this only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then you are again in contact with our X, you received the rifle from him, and is it true that he again refused to testify before the Court about the way he had obtained the rifle? Is it true that you then decided not to question him about that again?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you informed the Prosecutor's Office about that, was it then that a decision was made that you would be the one to testify before this Trial Chamber instead of this X and that you would say to the Trial Chamber what he had said to you? Was it at that point that the decision was made?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: The decision was made. But at what point exactly, I can't say any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did X authorise you to speak on his behalf before this Trial Chamber and testify as to how he had obtained this rifle? Did he authorise you?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Not with so many words. But he told me that -- I told him that it would be presented in the court most likely, and he asked me not to mention his name in public when it was represented.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was precisely my question. Did he authorise you to speak on his behalf and tell this story, or did he forbid you to mention his name in front of this Trial Chamber? So what did he do: Did he forbid you to mention his name, or did he authorise to tell the story on his behalf? Which was it?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: He did not forbid me to mention his name. He kindly requested not to use his name in public. I did not discuss the matter with him, whether I was allowed for him to tell the story in the courtroom or not. But he must have understood that it was going to be used, especially -- and you can have read it in my declaration, because I went through what he told me about the rifle so I would be sure that these were his words, what he said to me; I would not be mistaken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does he now know that you are testifying before this Trial Chamber? Have you had contacts with him recently? Have you informed him about that recently?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I have not spoken with him recently, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were considering this issue and the issue of your testimony, and when the decision was made that you would tell the story instead of Mr. X, was it then also considered -- why was it that X refused to testify? Was it maybe mentioned that he might be held responsible for perhaps giving a false testimony before this Trial Chamber? Was that also one of the considerations when the decision was being made about you testifying before this Trial Chamber instead of the -- of Mr. X?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. But I'm required to say the decisions about what evidence to lead in the courtroom are made by the attorneys, and the decision that was ultimately made by me. So I'm afraid that if Mr. Par at some point would like to have a discussion with me, we can do that. But this witness did not make the decision and cannot give the reasons for the decision, because that was made by the attorneys on the trial team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay. Well, Mr. Par, maybe you did not express your ideas very clearly, your question. You may put it another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Bos, did you have any reasons to believe that Mr. X didn't want to testify because he didn't want to utter a lie that would have exposed him to criminal proceedings? Did you maybe -- did that maybe occur to you? Did you maybe say that to somebody?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Isn't this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is the question what she thinks the witness might have thought? Isn't this speculation as to what the witness might have thought? Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. It's kind of speculation. Just ask very plainly how do you know or why did Mr. X refuse to testify in this courtroom. Just a neutral one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please answer the question that His Honour helped me to rephrase. According to you, do you have any opinion as to why Mr. X refused to testify before this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: He told me in November and in January that he was not up to testifying. He didn't feel well. And as I remember, he also mentioned something about security for his children. But there was another occasion when he was asked to testify, and that was done by my colleague, who went on mission before I went the last time, and I think he went on mission in August -- last August. He was also assigned to see the witness and ask him to testify. He met the witness, and the witness refused again.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: The witness refused again and stressed to my colleague that again for security reasons, he had children and he didn't want to testify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he at that point given an option to have protection measures granted to him, the customary protection measures before this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: When I spoke with him in January, in the end he said, "Okay. I will testify only if I can be relocated to the Netherlands." I told him that that probably is not going to be the case, the Tribunal is not relocated so many people. So that is it. He otherwise would not testify. That's what he said at that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand this part of your answer. You said that the Tribunal cannot relocate so many people. What exactly did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: The Tribunal is very careful and only relocates, as far as I know, relocate as few number -- a few people, a small number of people if needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In these proceedings, do you perhaps know how many people have been given this possibility of relocation by the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, this question is out of the scope.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we are discussing the conversation between Mr. X and our witness. They were talking about the conditions under which he would testify. What I would like to know here is whether this person blackmailed prosecutors, did he want to gain something by giving evidence, and this was just a normal conversation between the investigator and the person -- a potential witness. So this is a method that I didn't know anything about, and this is something I would really like to know more about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- yes. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I respectfully submit we have now gone beyond the scope of full cross-examination, to what counsel is entitled to what's classically known as a fishing expedition. If we need to talk -- if someone -- about various options afforded to people since 1993 by this institution, some of whom had been located to third -- relocated to third countries, that is not, respectfully, a question for this witness. That decision is made by the head of the victim and witness section, by the head of security, and by the chief of inspection of the OTP, not this witness, not this witness at all. She's not in a position nor should she be, to talk about the policy of relocating a very small number of very sensitive people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, you may put your question another way, but your previous question sounds like you are doing an investigation on the practice of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, we are not getting translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Bos, in very short line, can you tell us about your conversation between Mr. X and yourself regarding his possible relocation to a third country, if he decided to give his testimony in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: Sir, it was very short. He had already been refusing to give a signed statement, already refusing to testify. He then in the end say, "Okay, I will testify if I can be relocated to the Netherlands." And I said, "Sir, that's highly unlikely to happen."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you convey his request to the authorised persons in the Tribunal? Did you tell them about his conditions? Was that discussed at any time?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I remember I conveyed it to the trial team, but I cannot recall the discussion about it. As I remember, I think we all knew that that was most likely not going to happen, relocation for the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he -- today is he in a third country, or is he in his own country? You are the witness here. Maybe you are aware of his whereabouts at this moment. Do you know where he is?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: As far as I know, he is still in his own country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you ever heard, have you checked whether the 300 marks that he wanted was paid to him by the AID, or maybe you have never again discussed that issue with anybody?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: There's for me no reason to discuss this subject, so I did not discuss this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me be more precise. He never again asked for money in order for him to give you the rifle but that first time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: When I saw him again in January, as I told you already, he wanted to think about it because I told him I was not going to pay, and he told me to return after two days. That's all I can say about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's put Mr. X aside. Let's go back to Witness PP. You have obtained the rifle. You then went to Sarajevo to show him the rifle, to see whether maybe he would recognise it. Where did this take place in Sarajevo? Where did you show him the rifle? Where exactly?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: This happened in our Sarajevo field office in Sarajevo, as I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you find him in Sarajevo? Did you find him through the AID, through the local authorities? How did he get into your office?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: As I remember, I phoned him myself through my interpreter and made an appointment for him to come to the office, which he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you call him? Do you remember? Did you call him at home, or did you call him at his workplace?

utterances.speaker: APOLONIA BOS
utterances.text: I called him at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where he works?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, first, you know, we know that Witness PP is a protected witness, so -- so I think you have to refrain from asking some questions which concern his personal data. The other matter is that is that a relevant question, Mr. Par? Your cross-examination has gone for quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought it would be shorter. Unfortunately it hasn't been -- first, about the relevance of this question: I believe that this question is relevant for the following reason: The witness, who originally didn't identify the rifle was given the rifle for subsequent identification. I believe that that person may have been put under a lot of pressure in order to change his original testimony. I'm trying to establish whether he also was brought by the AID or whether his institution, the institution where he worked, may have also put pressure on him. And this, I believe, was the relevance of that question that I've just put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that this is all of your speculation, Mr. Par. Do you have any evidence to prove that? You said you believe that, you believe that. But you have -- you should have, you know, some evidence, you know, so that you could pursue it on this way, otherwise it's just a speculation that will get us nowhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honours. I do have evidence, and this is what I'm trying to establish through the witness. This witness said that he had carried a black rifle, and then he recognised the rifle which was shown to him. The colour didn't matter any more. For me there is a lot of room for concern. How come that one thing that was said originally can subsequently be changed? I believe that somebody must have put pressure on the witness. Secondly, the witness eventually didn't come here to confirm what he said. If a witness decides to act in that way, I believe that this is because he was pressurised in order to change his original testimony. I am not speculating. I am just basing my opinion on indisputable facts, on fact 1 and fact 2. Can I please proceed so that we don't -- that I don't waste any more time.
